articles.title: Council Votes on After-school Reading Program After Long Debate
articles.deck: Residents of Canal Park filled the hall on Thursday to ask questions about the plan.
body: Vera Esposito, who has lived in Canal Park for 33 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. The plan calls for after-school reading program along Bramble Terrace, with work expected to start in July.
Public works estimates the work will take about 33 weeks once it begins.
Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Thursday mornings. The group has raised $25,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

articles.title: Mariana Prentice, 77, Longtime Volunteer
articles.deck: Friends remember Mariana Prentice for the many years of service to Eastgate.
body: Mariana Prentice died in August at home on Willow Street, at the age of 77. Born in Eastgate in the years after the war, Mariana Prentice spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.

Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Eastgate Volunteer Fire Co. in his or her name. Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Eastgate.

body: Children are welcome, and volunteers will be on hand to help with parking and set-up. The event will be held at the Eastgate community hall, rain or shine, with a backup date set for the following Saturday.
Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public. Organizers ask guests to bring a dish to share or a little cash for supplies.

articles.title: Letter: The Stormwater Drain Repair on Walnut Road Needs Attention
body: To the editor: I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the December meeting.
Please keep the stormwater drain repair in the budget. Many of us on Walnut Road use it every week. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.
To the editor: I have lived on Walnut Road for 6 years, and I want to say what a difference the Foundry Row Mutual Aid Group has made.
Hal Hartigan, Marsh Landing

articles.deck: The vote came after 21 residents spoke at Thursday’s session.
body: Councilmember Gwen Dalrymple asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $12,000. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.
The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first.
